models.description:
todo app actors table.

This table stores core information about users who can authenticate and use the todo application. It contains credential information for authentication as well as profile data that is visible to the user. All todos and related data in the system belong to a specific user from this table.

The table implements email-based authentication with password hashing for security. Each user has a unique email address that serves as their login identifier. Profile information includes a display name that can be updated by the user.

Users in this table can create, view, edit, and delete their own todos. They have full control over their data including the ability to permanently delete their account, which removes all associated todos, history, and other personal data from the system.
models.name: todo_app_todo_users

plainFields.description: User's email address used for authentication and communication. Must be unique across all users in the system.
plainFields.name: email

plainFields.description: Hashed password for user authentication. Uses bcrypt hashing for security.
plainFields.name: password

plainFields.description: User's display name that appears in the application interface. Can be updated by the user as needed.
plainFields.name: display_name

plainFields.description: Timestamp when the user account was initially created.
plainFields.name: created_at

plainFields.description: Timestamp when the user account was last updated.
plainFields.name: updated_at

models.description:
JWT session tokens for user authentication with access and refresh token support for todo users.

This table manages authentication sessions for todo app users, storing both access and refresh tokens
with their expiration times. It maintains client connection metadata and tracks session usage for
security auditing. Each session is tied to a specific user and supports token refresh workflows.

The table implements secure session management with automatic expiration and last usage tracking.
It enforces uniqueness constraints on both access and refresh tokens to prevent conflicts. Sessions
are linked to users through the todo_app_todo_user_id foreign key with a one-to-many relationship,
enabling users to have multiple concurrent sessions.
models.name: todo_app_todo_user_sessions

plainFields.description: Access token for authentication
plainFields.name: access_token

plainFields.description: Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens
plainFields.name: refresh_token

plainFields.description: IP address of the client when the session was created
plainFields.name: ip

plainFields.description: User agent string of the client when the session was created
plainFields.name: user_agent

plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was created
plainFields.name: created_at

plainFields.description: Timestamp when the access token expires
plainFields.name: access_token_expires_at

plainFields.description: Timestamp when the refresh token expires
plainFields.name: refresh_token_expires_at

plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was last used
plainFields.name: last_used_at

models.description:
Password reset tokens with expiration for secure user password recovery workflow in the todo application.

This table manages the password reset process for todo users, storing unique tokens that are emailed to users when they request a password reset. Each token has an expiration time after which it becomes invalid. The table links to the main user account for verification during the reset process.

The tokens are designed to be single-use - once a password reset is completed using a token, that token is removed from this table. Expired tokens are also regularly cleaned up to maintain table performance.

When users successfully reset their password, the related entries in this table are automatically deleted as part of the password reset completion process.

foreignFields.description: Reference to the todo user who requested the password reset. Links to the main user account that the reset token is valid for. {@link todo_app_todo_users.id}
foreignFields.name: todo_user_id

models.name: todo_app_todo_user_password_resets

plainFields.description: Cryptographically secure random token string sent to the user's email address. Used to authenticate the password reset request. Should be sufficiently long and random to prevent guessing attacks.
plainFields.name: reset_token

plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset token expires. After this time, the token becomes invalid and cannot be used for password reset. Typically set to a short duration (e.g., 1 hour) from creation time.
plainFields.name: expires_at

plainFields.description: When this password reset record was created. Used for tracking token age and debugging purposes.
plainFields.name: created_at

models.description:
Email verification tokens for user registration confirmation in the todo application.

This table stores email verification tokens generated when a new user registers. Each token is associated with a specific user and has an expiration time. Once a user clicks the verification link containing this token, their email is confirmed and they can fully access the application. The token is then invalidated.

Tokens are automatically cleaned up after expiration to maintain database performance. The system ensures tokens are cryptographically secure and single-use to prevent security vulnerabilities.

foreignFields.description: The todo user associated with this email verification token. {@link todo_app_todo_users.id}
foreignFields.name: todo_app_todo_user_id

models.name: todo_app_todo_user_email_verifications

plainFields.description: Cryptographically secure token value used for email verification. This is a unique, random string that is emailed to the user as part of a verification link.
plainFields.name: code

plainFields.description: Expiration timestamp for the email verification token. After this time, the token becomes invalid and the user must request a new verification email.
plainFields.name: expired_at

plainFields.description: Timestamp when the email verification token was created.
plainFields.name: created_at

models.description:
Application configuration settings that control global behavior and feature flags for the todo application. 

This table stores system-wide configuration values that can be used to enable or disable features, 
set application limits, define operational parameters, and control other global behaviors. 
The configuration uses a key-value structure where each key represents a specific setting 
and the value contains the configuration data in JSON format.

Configurations are identified by unique keys and can be scoped to specific namespaces 
for better organization. The system maintains version history for configuration changes 
and includes temporal fields for audit trails.
models.name: todo_app_configurations

plainFields.description: Unique key identifying the configuration setting. Must follow naming conventions with lowercase letters, numbers, and underscores only. Examples: 'feature_enable_edit_history', 'limit_max_todos_per_user', 'auth_password_min_length'.
plainFields.name: key

plainFields.description: Namespace for organizing configurations. Allows grouping related settings together. Examples: 'auth', 'todo', 'system', 'limits'.
plainFields.name: namespace

plainFields.description: JSON-formatted configuration value. Can store simple values like strings and numbers, or complex objects and arrays as needed for the specific configuration setting.
plainFields.name: value

plainFields.description: Description of what this configuration setting does and how it should be used. Provides context for system administrators managing configurations.
plainFields.name: description

plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration entry was created. Used for audit trails and tracking when settings were introduced.
plainFields.name: created_at

plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration entry was last updated. Used for audit trails and tracking when settings were modified.
plainFields.name: updated_at

plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration entry was deleted (soft delete). Allows configuration entries to be archived without permanent removal.
plainFields.name: deleted_at

models.description:
todo_app_system_settings

This table stores key-value pairs of system configuration settings, including feature flags, operational parameters, and behavioral configurations that control the overall application functionality. Each setting is uniquely identified by its name and contains serialized value data along with descriptive metadata.

Settings are versioned through the todo_app_system_setting_histories table to maintain an audit trail of all changes.

Use this table to store configuration parameters that affect the entire application, such as:
- Feature enablement flags
- Performance tuning parameters
- Integration endpoint configurations
- Business rule thresholds
- Operational mode settings
models.name: todo_app_system_settings

plainFields.description: Unique name identifier for the setting, used as the lookup key for configuration values.
plainFields.name: name

plainFields.description: Serialized value of the setting, stored as a string representation of the actual data type.
plainFields.name: value

plainFields.description: Human-readable description explaining the purpose and usage of this system setting.
plainFields.name: description

plainFields.description: Timestamp when the setting was initially created in the system.
plainFields.name: created_at

plainFields.description: Timestamp when the setting was last modified.
plainFields.name: updated_at

models.description:
Tracking table for database schema versions and migration history in the todo application.

This table maintains a chronological record of all schema changes applied to the application database. Each entry represents a specific version of the database schema, allowing for reliable migration management and rollback capabilities when needed.

The version tracking system ensures that database changes are applied consistently across different environments (development, staging, production) and provides audit trails for schema evolution. It supports automated migration workflows by recording which migrations have been applied and when.

Each version entry includes metadata about the migration such as version identifier, description, and timestamps for when the migration was applied. The system prevents duplicate migrations by enforcing unique version identifiers.
models.name: todo_app_schema_versions

plainFields.description: Primary human-readable identifier for this schema version. Typically follows semantic versioning patterns (e.g., v1.0.0) or migration naming conventions (e.g., 20241201153000_initial_setup).
plainFields.name: version

plainFields.description: Brief description of what changes this schema version introduces. Explains the purpose and impact of the migration for operational understanding.
plainFields.name: description

plainFields.description: Timestamp when this schema version was applied to the database. Used for migration ordering and audit trail purposes.
plainFields.name: applied_at

models.name: todo_app_todos
models.description:
Main todo items created by users in the todo application, containing all core metadata including title, description, and temporal fields for task management.

This table represents the primary business entity for the todo application where users store their task items. Each todo is owned by a specific user who is authenticated through the todo_app_todo_users relationship.

Key aspects of this table include:

- Complete ownership tracking through foreign key relationships to user accounts
- Soft deletion support for the trash system
- Full temporal tracking with created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at timestamps
- Status tracking with completed boolean field
- Proper indexing strategy for common query patterns

The table is designed to support all user operations including:

- Viewing personal todo lists with pagination
- Creating new todos with optional metadata
- Updating todos with full edit history tracking (handled by History component)
- Soft deleting todos which moves them to trash (handled by Trash component)
- Filtering and sorting todos by various criteria
- Permanent relationship with user owners for privacy enforcement

foreignFields.name: todo_app_todo_user_id
foreignFields.description: Owner of this todo item. {@link todo_app_todo_users.id}.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Concise summary of what needs to be done. This is the primary identifier users see in their todo lists.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed explanation or additional context for the todo item. May contain formatting or extended information.

plainFields.name: start_date
plainFields.description: When the user plans to start working on this todo. Used for sorting and filtering todos by start date.

plainFields.name: due_date
plainFields.description: Deadline by which this todo should be completed. Critical for sorting, filtering, and priority management.

plainFields.name: completed
plainFields.description: Whether this todo has been marked as complete by the user. This is the primary status indicator for filtering.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When this todo was originally created by the user. Used for chronological sorting and filtering.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: When this todo was last modified by the user. Used for sorting by recent activity.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: When this todo was moved to trash (soft delete). Null means active todo, non-null means in trash.

models.name: todo_app_todo_edit_histories
models.description:
Records all edit history entries for todos, capturing detailed information about every change made to a todo including which fields were modified and when.

Each history entry represents a single edit event on a todo item and captures the changes to specific fields (title, description, start date, due date). This table provides a complete audit trail of all modifications made to todos over time, which is essential for tracking changes, recovering previous versions, and understanding how todos evolve.

History entries are immutable once created and are associated with both the todo being modified and the user session that performed the edit. The system only creates entries when actual changes occur - if a user submits an edit request without making any actual changes to field values, no history entry is created.

foreignFields.name: todo_app_todo_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the todo item that was edited. {@link todo_app_todos.id}

foreignFields.name: todo_app_todo_user_session_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the user session that performed this edit. {@link todo_app_todo_user_sessions.id}

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: The updated title of the todo item. Only present if the title was changed in this edit.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: The updated description of the todo item. Only present if the description was changed in this edit.

plainFields.name: start_date
plainFields.description: The updated start date of the todo item. Only present if the start date was changed in this edit.

plainFields.name: due_date
plainFields.description: The updated due date of the todo item. Only present if the due date was changed in this edit.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this edit history entry was created. This represents the exact moment when the edit occurred.

models.description:
Records all soft-deleted todos, preserving complete todo data and metadata at the time of deletion for potential restoration or permanent removal.

This table captures all information about todos when they are moved to the trash. It maintains the exact state of the todo at deletion time, including all fields like title, description, dates, and completion status. This enables full restoration of deleted todos while keeping them separate from active todos.

Key relationships:
- Belongs to a user who created the original todo
- Maintains reference to original todo data for restoration
- Contains all metadata needed to reconstruct the original todo if restored

This table supports the trash system functionality by:
1. Storing complete todo data when soft deleted
2. Providing data for trash listing views
3. Enabling full restoration of deleted todos
4. Supporting permanent deletion workflows

foreignFields.description: The user who created this todo. {@link todo_app_todo_users.id}
foreignFields.name: todo_app_todo_user_id

foreignFields.description: The original todo that was moved to trash. {@link todo_app_todos.id}
foreignFields.name: todo_app_todo_id

models.name: todo_app_trash_entries

plainFields.description: The title of the todo at the time it was moved to trash. Preserves the original title for potential restoration.
plainFields.name: title

plainFields.description: The description of the todo at the time it was moved to trash. Preserves the original description for potential restoration.
plainFields.name: description

plainFields.description: The start date of the todo at the time it was moved to trash. Preserves the original start date for potential restoration.
plainFields.name: start_at

plainFields.description: The due date of the todo at the time it was moved to trash. Preserves the original due date for potential restoration.
plainFields.name: end_at

plainFields.description: Whether the todo was marked complete at the time it was moved to trash. Preserves the original completion status for potential restoration.
plainFields.name: completed_at

plainFields.description: When the todo was originally created, preserved from the original todo for accurate historical tracking.
plainFields.name: created_at

plainFields.description: When the todo was last updated before being moved to trash, preserved from the original todo for accurate historical tracking.
plainFields.name: updated_at

plainFields.description: When the todo was moved to trash. This timestamp enables sorting of trash entries by deletion time and supports time-based trash management operations.
plainFields.name: deleted_at

models.name: todo_app_permanent_deletion_records
models.description:
Records of todos that have been permanently deleted from the trash system.

This table tracks all todos that have been permanently removed from the system by users. When a user chooses to permanently delete a todo from their trash, a record is created in this table containing a reference to the original todo and the timestamp of deletion. This provides an audit trail of all permanent deletions for compliance and recovery purposes.

The table is append-only with no updates or deletions allowed after creation. This ensures a complete and immutable history of all permanent deletions.

Key relationships:
- References the original todo through the todo_app_todos.id foreign key
- Provides a complete log of user-initiated permanent deletions

foreignFields.name: todo_app_todo_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the original todo that was permanently deleted. {@link todo_app_todos.id}

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when the todo was permanently deleted by the user.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when this permanent deletion record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp of the last update to this record.
